On June 9, he came home from a show, put his animals away, and noticed one cooler was empty. Irwin, his 2-foot alligator, was gone. Here's the thing: neighbors say this is the THIRD alligator to escape from the property. Not the first. Not the second. The third. Previous escapees from Mark's Ark include a pony, a tortoise, a pig, and an emu. The county is searching. Kohlhorst says Irwin is small and harmless — a 2-foot gator poses no danger. His neighbor says a 2-foot alligator could take your fingers off. Irwin is still at large. If a 2-foot alligator showed up in your yard, would you trust the owner's word?

05_yoon-suk-yeol-30-years.json.title: He Flew Drones Over North Korea to Justify Martial Law. 30 Years.
05_yoon-suk-yeol-30-years.json.script: A president ordered what? South Korea's Yoon Suk Yeol — who declared emergency martial law in December 2024 — just got 30 years in prison. And here's why: prosecutors proved Yoon secretly ordered the military to fly surveillance drones over Pyongyang, North Korea's capital, hoping to provoke a military reaction that would justify the martial law. His defense minister, Kim Yong Hyun, got 30 years alongside him. The Seoul Central District Court called it a deliberate abuse of authority for personal political gain. Yoon appealed immediately. The whole scheme depended on North Korea reacting to a military provocation it never actually knew about. If those surveillance drones had caused an incident — would anyone have questioned the martial law?

06_charlevoix-michigan-lottery.json.title: She Thought the Lottery Scanner Was Broken. It Wasn't.
06_charlevoix-michigan-lottery.json.script: Broken scanner. Or $2.2 million? A 66-year-old woman from Charlevoix County, Michigan had an urge to buy a lottery ticket — Millionaire for Life from the Michigan Lottery. She scanned it at a store. A message came up: contact the lottery office. She figured the machine was broken. Walked to her car. Looked up the Michigan Lottery website. Her 5 numbers — 03, 15, 16, 24, 28 — matched the May 21 drawing. Not broken. She won $100,000 a year for life. She chose the lump sum: $2.2 million. The winning ticket was from the Mancelona North EZ Mart. She stayed anonymous. She's buying a house, a car, and a boat. If your lottery scanner said contact the lottery office, would you assume it was broken?
